AfterDeath.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30. The guards are exact -- `target != base.Owner && target.Side == base.Owner.Side && !base.Owner.IsDead` (RavenousPower.cs:26) maps line-for-line to powers.py:1931-1935 -- and the effect order matches (stun the owner, then grant Strength). Two divergences named, both now settled dormant. (1) MISSING `applier=` on the Strength grant (RavenousPower.cs:33 passes `base.Owner`, powers.py:1939 omits it) is the SAME site as this record's own `power/ravenous/g1` guard, already verdicted `gap`/dormant with an executed enumeration of every `applier`-reader in the sim (RitualPower, `_PossessPower._track`, UnsettlingLamp, the shrink/constrict/dampen/hex on_death applier tests) -- none matches an enemy self-buff with a positive delta, per `py audit/tools/gap_queue.py list | grep ravenous` (`power/ravenous/g1 ... dormant`). Not re-verdicted here; cited for rule-3 consistency, not re-derived. (2) The `((CorpseSlug)base.Owner.Monster).IsRavenous` flag (RavenousPower.cs:31, cleared in StunnedMove at :41) is settled here, EXECUTED: `grep -rln IsRavenous "Slay the Spire 2/src"` returns exactly two files, `CorpseSlug.cs` (the declaration, `_isRavenous`/`IsRavenous` at lines 35/57-66) and `RavenousPower.cs` (the two writes at :31/:41) -- no third file reads it. Within `CorpseSlug.cs` itself the only READS of `_isRavenous` are five `creatureAnimator.AddAnyState(...)` predicates (lines 169-175) selecting which Hit/Dead/DevourStart animation clip plays -- pure presentation, the same class already waived on this very record as the 'TriggerAnim DevourStart/DevourEnd' guard ('Presentation only'). No move-selection branch, no intent, no combat-state read consults it. So the sim's omission of an IsRavenous-equivalent flag is DORMANT: the flag is provably unobservable outside animation in the decompiled source itself, not merely unread by ported content. VERIFIED by reading RavenousPower.cs, CorpseSlug.cs in full and re-grepping the whole C# source tree for the symbol.
